name: SWE-bench/SWE-bench
why: The benchmark harness itself: containerised Docker evaluation with fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests as the grader spec. Lesson from its issue #465 (closed): agents ran `git log --all` in the sandbox to read future fix commits, so the images were rebuilt; scrub git history and future refs from every task sandbox

name: SWE-agent/SWE-agent
why: Reference agent behind H10; whole agent is governed by one YAML config and runs are saved as trajectories. Its README now says mini-swe-agent has superseded it and matches its performance: borrow the single-config, trajectory-per-run habit, and expect heavy scaffolds to be replaced by lean ones as models improve

name: SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent
why: ~100-line bash-only agent with a linear message history and one subprocess per action (trivially sandboxed); README claims >74% on SWE-bench Verified (their claim). Use as the minimal-scaffold baseline arm in our benchmark; its README states the lesson that special tools matter less as models improve (compare C12 scaffold study)

name: OpenHands/OpenHands
why: C4's platform: sandboxed runtime plus an evaluation harness covering SWE-bench and other benchmarks. Borrow its split of agent, runtime sandbox and per-benchmark evaluation code, and its practice of reporting one agent across many task types

name: OpenAutoCoder/Agentless
why: C3's fixed three-phase pipeline (localise, repair, validate) with generated reproduction tests used to re-rank patches. Borrow the reproduction-test-then-select step; note C2 shows it scored 0% on JavaScript until its Python parser was swapped, and the repo has had no push since 2024-12

name: microsoft/SWE-bench-Live
why: Continuously refreshed task set (monthly additions) with an explicit protocol: the agent sees only problem_statement and the docker image, prompts may not hold instance-specific solutions, and submissions must include raw trajectories so maintainers can audit compliance. Borrow the protocol text and the trajectory-audit rule for our benchmark

name: scaleapi/SWE-bench_Pro-os
why: C9/C12 benchmark. V2 ships a locked protocol: offline agent phase, fresh-container re-grade of the patch, and an oracle run proving reference patches pass 642/642. Borrow the oracle and empty-patch sanity checks and the clean-container grading; its news log (leaderboard issues, removed outdated tests) is a record of benchmark maintenance

name: SWE-bench/experiments
why: Submission repo for the leaderboards: one metadata.yaml per entry, artifacts kept in the submitter's repo, and (since 2025-11-18) a rule that Verified/Multilingual entries need an open publication. Borrow the entries-not-artifacts layout for our scorecards; no license, so read only

name: SWE-bench/SWE-smith
why: Turns any repo into runnable tasks: build env, synthesise task instances, keep those that break at least one unit test, generate issue text. Borrow the keep-only-tasks-that-fail-a-test filter if the kit's benchmark needs generated app tasks

name: SWE-Gym/SWE-Gym
why: Training environments plus inference-time verifier scaling (context for retries). Its README carries a 'patch before use' warning about the same git shortcut as SWE-bench #465 to prevent reward hacking: lesson that every task image must be audited before use

name: ScalingIntelligence/codemonkeys
why: C10's code: pipeline split into context, generation and selection scripts, with a step that reproduces the paper figures and a selector that can combine candidates from other systems. Borrow the stage-per-script layout and the figures-from-saved-outputs habit

name: QwenLM/qwen-code
why: The harness C11 measured across 35 releases (no significant resolve-rate gain, nearly double the tokens). Lesson: pin the agent-harness version and rerun a fixed task sample on every upgrade, as a regression test for the harness itself

name: harbor-framework/harbor
why: Framework that runs arbitrary agents (including claude-code) on tasks in one container format with a verifier, in parallel; SWE-Bench Pro V2 ships as Harbor tasks. Candidate runner for our own benchmark; check fit with `claude plugin eval` before adopting

name: openai/frontier-evals
why: Holds the SWE-Lancer eval (real freelance tasks graded by end-to-end tests, per its README). Borrow the idea of grading by user-visible end-to-end tests rather than unit tests; the SWE-Lancer paper itself is not fetched in this folder
